name: Jagadeeswarar Temple, Tiruppereyil (Ogai Perayur)
deity: Shiva as Jagadeeswarar (lord of the universe), with the goddess Jagan Nayaki (Pennamirtha Nayaki)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Ogai Perayur, the Tevaram's Tiruppereyil, near Tiruvarur, honours Shiva as Jagadeeswarar — the lord of the universe — with the goddess Jagan Nayaki. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Appar, it is remembered as a fortified place (pereyil, 'great rampart') of the early Chola age, when Tiruvarur was a seat of the empire.

sections.history: Tiruppereyil, now the village of Ogai Perayur, lies about 13 km from Tiruvarur and some 21 km from Mannargudi, in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirunavukkarasar (Appar). The name Pereyil, 'the great rampart,' recalls a tradition that the place was a fort in the early Chola age, when Tiruvarur was a seat of the Chola power. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later; little of its fuller sthala purana survives.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Jagadeeswarar — 'lord of the universe' — in the sanctum, with the goddess Jagan Nayaki, also called Pennamirtha Nayaki, in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The sthala vriksham is the narthai (citron) tree, and the sacred tank is the Agni Theertham.
sections.legends: The lord's name Jagadeeswarar, 'the ruler of the world,' and the goddess Jagan Nayaki, 'the lady of the world,' make this a shrine of the universal sovereignty of Shiva and Devi. The goddess is also praised as Pennamirtha Nayaki, 'she who is the nectar among women.' Little of the older sthala purana is recorded, so the shrine's devotion is carried chiefly by its names and by Appar's Tevaram verses.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps Margazhi Tiruvadhirai in Margazhi (December–January), Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail near Tiruvarur include Ogai Perayur among their stops.
sections.experience: At Ogai Perayur the pilgrim comes to the shrine of the lord and lady of the universe, in a village that remembers an old rampart of the Chola age. Before Jagadeeswarar and Jagan Nayaki, beside the Agni Theertham, the visitor finds the universal sovereignty of Shiva kept in a quiet Tevaram temple of the Tiruvarur country.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Ogai Perayur (Tiruppereyil) is about 13 km from Tiruvarur and 21 km from Mannargudi, in Tiruvarur district. Tiruvarur is the nearest rail head, with buses and taxis to the village.
